subject: Re: Order form inspection triggers & rolling evidence windows
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@veridian.com>, compliance@veridian.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form inspection triggers & rolling evidence windows

Emily — thanks for walking through Veridian's intake checklist this morning. Attaching our proposed redlines for the Order Form and a companion evidence cadence matrix (see attachments). High-level asks from Veridian that we want to address in the MSA/Order Form: a) clear inspection trigger language, b) a rolling evidence window with scoped log/export delivery, and c) pen-test notice timing and staging access limits.

Proposed positions we're putting on the table:
- Inspection triggers: keep to "material security incident" + contractually scoped compliance audits (SOC 2) — avoid open-ended "any reason" inspection.
- Rolling evidence window: provide a 30-day rolling bundle of requested artifacts (logs, config snapshots, SOC2 report excerpts) on a scheduled cadence rather than ad-hoc exports.
- Pen-test / staging: 30-day notice for scheduled penetration tests, with a single 72-hour weekend staging window and ephemeral credentials; production access only by mutually-agreed forensic process.

Can you confirm whether Veridian needs a longer notice window for pen-tests (Emily mentioned 45 days) and whether the rolling bundle cadence (weekly summarized bundle, full export monthly) meets their control requirements? If we can align on those two bullets, Karthik can draft targeted MSA/Order Form language.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_orderform_redlines.pdf (pdf), evidence_cadence_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@veridian.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@veridian.com
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form inspection triggers & rolling evidence windows

Thanks, Soojin — useful start. A few clarifications from Veridian's side:

1) Pen-test notice: standard internal policy asks for 45 calendar days for full-scope tests so we can coordinate executive/ops on our end. We can accept a shorter window for patch/defensive-only tests, but for anything involving active scanning we typically require 45 days.

2) Rolling evidence: the 30-day rolling bundle sounds reasonable if it includes indexed logs (application + auth events) and a minimal set of config artifacts. We prefer a weekly deliverable with a monthly full export for our internal auditors.

3) Inspection triggers: Veridian will push for language that allows inspection "on reasonable notice" in addition to breaches — can we propose a middle ground: a standing quarterly assurance review by mutually-agreed scope (unless a material incident arises)?

Emily Rogers
VP, Security & Compliance
Veridian Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@veridian.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form inspection triggers & rolling evidence windows

Emily / team — thanks for the quick feedback. A few legal points and a compromise proposal below.

On pen-test notice:
- We can accept a 45-day notice for full-scope external tests. For low-impact or internal vulnerability assessments we want to retain the ability to accept shorter notice (30 days) subject to operational approval. I'll add carveouts for emergency patching and pre-authorized vendor lists.

On rolling evidence and inspections:
- Instead of open "reasonable notice" language, propose: (i) quarterly assurance reviews (mutually agreed scope) as a standing right; (ii) ad-hoc inspections limited to material incidents or written justification tying the inspection to a specific control gap; (iii) for audit-type activities we will provide a 30-day rolling evidence bundle (weekly indexed summaries + monthly exports) for a 12-month lookback.
- For log data we will supply hashed/filtered export where appropriate and a controls matrix crosswalk to SOC 2 assertions to protect customer data minimization requirements.

Operational constraints / safeguard language to add:
- Timeboxed forensic access: any privileged access requires a signed Data Access Addendum, logged sessions, and a mutually-agreed sampling plan; forensic exports limited to scoped buckets and retained only for the duration required for the audit (then deleted).
- Staging window: propose a single 72-hour weekend window per scheduled test; additional windows by exception with written consent.

If that compromise is acceptable, I'll translate into redline language for the MSA and Order Form (we'll add the specific notice periods as parameters). Vanessa — can you confirm commercial impact if we accept a 45-day hard notice for full-scope pen-tests? Marcus — please confirm the feasibility of the weekly indexed summaries + monthly export from infra.

- Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form inspection triggers & rolling evidence windows

Quick ops confirmation:
- Weekly indexed summaries are implementable. We'll generate a compact CSV with indexed event counts and pointers to the monthly export objects (S3 URIs or ephemeral secure transfer).
- Monthly full export: we can provide up to a 12-month rolling window as a zipped export; we'll apply redaction rules and show a controls crosswalk.
- Pen-test staging: 72-hour weekend window is fine; we can support an extended 5-day window by exception if Veridian can provide a narrow scope and a dedicated ops contact.

I'll prepare a short ops note describing the exports and ephemeral credential flows for the Data Access Addendum.

Marcus Lin
VP, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
